title: Reweighting is not Harmless: Understanding the Role of Dataset Characteristics
abstract: arXiv:2611.07258v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reweighting is a widely used pre-processing method for promoting discrimination-free model behavior by assigning different weights to data points during model training. While it is often credited with improving fairness, particularly by mitigating systematic underestimation for underrepresented groups, it can also introduce unintended harms under certain data conditions. Using controlled simulations that vary group size and baseline event prevalence, we show how reweighting can yield misleading improvements in fairness by reducing underestimation for one group while introducing it for another. Across 3,000 simulated datasets with event prevalence of 7-14%, reweighting improved parity in positive classification and false negative rates (FNR) between groups, but did so partly by decreasing positive classifications and increasing FNR for the group with higher baseline prevalence. translated_title: 重加权并非无害：理解数据集特征的作用
translated_abstract: 重加权是一种广泛使用的预处理方法，通过在模型训练过程中为数据点分配不同的权重来促进无歧视的模型行为。虽然它通常被认为能改善公平性，特别是通过缓解对代表性不足群体的系统性低估，但在某些数据条件下，它也可能引入意想不到的危害。通过改变群体规模和基线事件发生率的受控模拟，我们展示了重加权如何通过减少一个群体的低估而在另一个群体中引入低估，从而产生误导性的公平性改善。在3,000个事件发生率为7-14%的模拟数据集中，重加权改善了群体间阳性分类和假阴性率（FNR）的均等性，但部分是通过减少基线发生率较高群体的阳性分类并增加其FNR来实现的。当该群体是少数群体时，这些效应最为明显。
tldr: 重加权虽然改善了群体间的公平性指标，但可能通过损害基线发生率较高（尤其是少数）群体的预测表现来实现，从而产生误导性的公平性改善。
en_tdlr: Reweighting can yield misleading fairness improvements by reducing underestimation for one group while introducing it for another, disproportionately harming minority groups with higher baseline event prevalence.
